Browsers ignore a `rel` value they don't know. A typo such as `rel="noopenner"` looks like it protects the link, but it does nothing.

The rule checks `rel` on HTML elements in JSX and in `React.createElement`. It reports:

- a value that isn't a link type at all, or isn't one for this element: `stylesheet` is for `<link>`, `noopener` is for `<a>`, `<area>` and `<form>`
- `rel` on an element other than `<a>`, `<area>`, `<form>` and `<link>`
- an empty `rel`, or one that isn't a string
- `shortcut` without `icon` after it
- extra whitespace around or between the values

The rule doesn't check your own components. Most reports come with a suggestion that removes the invalid part.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/no-invalid-html-attribute" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/no-invalid-html-attribute" = ["error", ["rel"]]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```jsx
const docs = <a href="https://example.com" rel="noopenner">Docs</a>;

const home = <a href="/" rel="stylesheet">Home</a>;

const logo = <img src="/logo.png" rel="preload" />;
```

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```jsx
const empty = <a href="/" rel="">Home</a>;

const spaced = <a href="https://example.com" rel="noopener  noreferrer">Docs</a>;

const icon = <link rel="shortcut" href="/favicon.ico" />;
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
const docs = <a href="https://example.com" rel="noopener noreferrer">Docs</a>;

const styles = <link rel="stylesheet" href="/main.css" />;

const icon = <link rel="shortcut icon" href="/favicon.ico" />;

const next = <PageLink rel="following" to="/page/2" />;
```

## Options

The option is the list of attributes to check. `"rel"` is the only attribute the rule knows, so the default is `["rel"]`.
